{{Recipe summary
| Category = Sauce recipes
| Difficulty = 2
}}

{{recipe}}

'''Nam phrik ong''', or ''Thai pork and tomato dip'' (Thai: น้ำพริกอ่อง), is a traditional Northern [[w:Thai food|Thai food]] of pork, tomatoes, and chilli. It is much like a Thai version of a bolognese sauce,<ref>{{cite web|title=Thai Nam Prik Ong|url=http://aroundtheworldtravels.co.uk/food-around-world/local-food-in-thailand/thai-nam-%20prik-%20ong/|work=Around the World Travels}}</ref> and the name comes from combining ''nam phrik'' (hot sauce; literally "liquid chili") and ''ong''. ''Ong'' is used only for identifying the dish, and has no special meaning<ref>{{cite web|title=Dondero: Sweet-spicy Nam Prik Ong is a Northern Thai treat|url=http://onlineathens.com/food/2012-07-17/dondero-sweet-spicy-nam-prik-ong-northern-thai-treat|work=Online Athens|publisher=Tim Dondero}}</ref>. The tomatoes and chilli colour the sauce orange, and the dish tastes sour, salty, and slightly hot. Some variations of the dish can be a little sweet, depending on preference. 

While tomatoes and pork are the essential main ingredients of Nam Phrik Ong, people may add other spices. The spices are not specific, and vary widely<ref>{{cite web|title=น้ำพริกอ่อง|url=http://library.cmu.ac.th/ntic/lannafood/detail_lannafood.php?id_food=27|work=Chiang Mai University Library}}</ref>. 

==Ingredients==
* 20 dried paprika [[Cookbook:Chiles|chile peppers]]
* 20 [[Cookbook:Shallot|shallots]]
* 10 [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]] cloves
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tbsp|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Shrimp paste|shrimp paste]]
* ½ [[Cookbook:Tsp|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] [[Cookbook:Cilantro|coriander leaves]]
* 1 tbsp sliced [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]
* 400 g [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]] or ground [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]
* 20 small [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]

==Procedure==
# Pound together the peppers, shallots, and garlic.
# Add the shrimp paste and salt, and continue pounding the mixture.
# Heat the oil in a pan, and add the pounded mixture. Stir in the coriander and onion. Cook until fragrant.
# Add the pork, and stir it until it is cooked. Add some water if it gets dry.
# Bring the mixture to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]].
# When the mixture is boiling, add the tomatoes and stir them around. Wait until they are cooked.
# Serve with some vegetables for dipping such as lettuce wraps, cabbage, and/or green beans.<ref>{{cite web |title=Thai-Style Lettuce Wraps - Nam Prik Ong - น้ำพริกอ่อง |url=http://thai-foodie.com/thaifood/thai-style-lettuce-wraps-nam-prik-ong-%E0%B8%99%E0%B9%89%E0%B8%B3%E0%B8%9E%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B4%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%AD%E0%B9%88%E0%B8%AD%E0%B8%87/ |work=Thai-Foodie |publisher=Sherri Pengjad}}</ref>
